text: Which structure in an animal cell is bounded by a single membrane and contains hydrolytic enzymes?
solution: Lysosomes are small sacs, each with one membrane, filled with digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes that break down worn-out organelles and engulfed material. Mitochondria have a double membrane; ribosomes, the nucleolus and centrioles have no membrane of their own.

text:
A cell is heterozygous for two genes that lie on the same chromosome. One chromosome of the pair carries alleles A and B; its homologue carries a and b.
If there is no crossing over and no mutation, which combinations of these alleles can a gamete made by meiosis carry?
options: A, a, B or b only
solution: Linked genes travel together on their chromosome. Meiosis puts one chromosome of each pair into each gamete, so a gamete gets either the A-B chromosome or the a-b one. Ab and aB need crossing over between the genes. A gamete is haploid, so it has one allele of each gene, never AaBb or a single allele.

text:
Where do transcription and translation take place in a eukaryotic cell?

| | transcription | translation |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | cytoplasm | nucleus |
| row 2 | nucleus | nucleus |
| row 3 | nucleus | ribosomes in the cytoplasm |
| row 4 | ribosomes | nucleus |
| row 5 | Golgi apparatus | ribosomes in the cytoplasm |
solution: DNA stays in the nucleus, so mRNA is transcribed there. The mRNA leaves through the nuclear pores and is translated on ribosomes in the cytoplasm (free or on the rough ER). Row 3. In prokaryotes, with no nucleus, both happen in the cytoplasm.

text:
Which row shows the features found in BOTH mRNA and DNA?

| | ribose | thymine | phosphate groups | cytosine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| row 1 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| row 2 | x | ✓ | ✓ | x |
| row 3 | ✓ | x | ✓ | ✓ |
| row 4 | x | x | ✓ | ✓ |
| row 5 | x | x | x | ✓ |

Key: ✓ found in both, x not found in both
solution: Both are chains of nucleotides joined through phosphate groups, and both use cytosine (with adenine and guanine). The differences: mRNA has ribose and uracil, DNA has deoxyribose and thymine. So ribose and thymine are each in only one of them. Row 4.

text:
Which of the following increase genetic variation within a population?
1 mutation
2 sexual reproduction, through meiosis and random fertilisation
3 directional selection
solution: Mutation is the only source of new alleles, and meiosis plus random fertilisation make new combinations of existing alleles. Selection does the opposite: by favouring one phenotype it removes alleles and narrows the variation. So 1 and 2 only.

text:
These steps are used to make human insulin in bacteria:
P: put the recombinant plasmids into bacteria
Q: obtain the human insulin gene
R: cut a plasmid with the same restriction enzyme used on the gene
S: join the gene into the plasmid with DNA ligase
T: grow the bacteria that took up the plasmid in a fermenter
Which order is correct?
solution: First get the gene (Q) and open the plasmid with the matching restriction enzyme (R), so both have the same sticky ends. Ligase then seals the gene in (S); only then can the recombinant plasmid be put into bacteria (P), which are selected and grown in bulk (T). Ligase cannot join a plasmid that has not been cut, and bacteria cannot take up a plasmid that does not exist yet.

text: Which sequence lists these from SMALLEST to LARGEST?
options: a bacterium → a virus → a human liver cell
a virus → a bacterium → a human liver cell
a human liver cell → a bacterium → a virus
a virus → a human liver cell → a bacterium
a bacterium → a human liver cell → a virus
solution: Typical sizes: a virus about 0.02-0.3 micrometres, a bacterium about 1-5 micrometres, a liver cell about 20-30 micrometres. Each step is roughly ten times larger.

text: Which organ makes insulin, and which organ stores much of the excess glucose that insulin helps remove from the blood, as glycogen?
options: the liver makes it; the pancreas stores glycogen
the pancreas makes it; the pancreas stores glycogen
the pancreas makes it; the liver stores glycogen
the adrenal glands make it; the liver stores glycogen
the liver makes it; the muscles store glycogen
solution: Insulin is made by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. It makes liver (and muscle) cells take up glucose and convert it to glycogen, which the liver stores and releases again when glucose falls. The pancreas makes the hormone but stores no glycogen to speak of.

text:
Which of the following are enzymes?
1 ATP synthase
2 NAD
3 ATP
solution: ATP synthase is a protein that catalyses the formation of ATP, so it is an enzyme (the -ase ending is the clue). NAD is a coenzyme: it carries hydrogen between enzymes but is not a catalyst. ATP is the energy-carrying molecule the enzyme makes. 1 only.

text:
A human cell with 46 chromosomes undergoes meiosis.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 At the end of meiosis I, each cell has 23 chromosomes, each made of two chromatids.
2 Each of the four cells produced has 23 chromosomes.
3 The four cells produced contain 92 chromosomes between them.
solution: Meiosis I separates the homologous pairs, so each cell has 23 chromosomes, still double (two chromatids each) (1). Meiosis II separates the chromatids, giving four cells of 23 single chromosomes (2). Four times 23 is 92, double the original 46, because the DNA was copied once before two divisions (3). All three.

text:
Two genes assort independently, and each shows complete dominance.
How many more phenotypes appear among the offspring of AaBb x AaBb than among the offspring of AaBb x AAbb?
solution: AaBb x AaBb: each gene gives both the dominant and the recessive phenotype, so 2 x 2 = 4 phenotypes. AaBb x AAbb: every child gets an A, so all show the dominant A phenotype, while Bb x bb still gives both B phenotypes: 1 x 2 = 2. The difference is 2.

text: Which option gives the site of the Krebs cycle (S), the main hydrogen carrier that the cycle reduces (H), and where that carrier takes its hydrogen next (D)?
options: S: cytoplasm; H: NAD; D: ATP synthase
S: mitochondrial matrix; H: NAD; D: the electron transport chain
S: mitochondrial matrix; H: NADP; D: the Calvin cycle
S: inner mitochondrial membrane; H: FAD; D: glycolysis
S: stroma; H: NADP; D: the electron transport chain
solution: The Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix and loads hydrogen mainly onto NAD (plus some FAD). Reduced NAD passes its electrons to the electron transport chain on the inner membrane. NADP is the carrier of photosynthesis, which runs in the chloroplast stroma and thylakoids.

text:
The stages of meiosis I are: prophase I → stage two → anaphase I → stage four.
Which row shows what happens in stage two and in stage four?

| | stage two | stage four |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | single chromosomes line up at the equator | sister chromatids reach the poles |
| row 2 | crossing over takes place | the spindle forms |
| row 3 | homologous pairs line up at the equator | a nucleus forms at each pole with half the chromosome number |
| row 4 | DNA replicates | the cytoplasm divides |
| row 5 | chromatids separate | homologous chromosomes pair up |
solution: Stage two is metaphase I, where homologous chromosomes line up in PAIRS on the equator; stage four is telophase I, when nuclei re-form with half the number of chromosomes (each still of two chromatids). Single chromosomes lining up and chromatids separating belong to meiosis II; crossing over is in prophase I and DNA replicates before meiosis starts.

text:
In which of these structures are lipids made or modified?
1 smooth endoplasmic reticulum
2 Golgi apparatus
3 ribosome
solution: The smooth ER makes lipids, including phospholipids and steroids. The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages them, for example adding carbohydrate to make glycolipids. Ribosomes make proteins only. So 1 and 2 only.

text:
Which of the following salts give an ACIDIC solution when dissolved in water?
1 \(\mathrm{NH_4Cl}\)
2 \(\mathrm{KNO_3}\)
3 \(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}\)
solution: Ammonium chloride comes from a weak base and a strong acid: \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) gives up a proton to water, so the solution is acidic. Potassium nitrate (strong base, strong acid) is neutral. Sodium ethanoate (strong base, weak acid) is alkaline, because ethanoate takes a proton from water. 1 only.

text:
Barium nitrate solution and sodium carbonate solution are mixed, and a white precipitate of barium carbonate forms; sodium nitrate stays dissolved.
Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
solution: Barium is in Group 2, so it forms \(\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}\); carbonate is \(\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}\). One of each balances the charges in \(\mathrm{BaCO_3}\). Sodium and nitrate are spectators that stay in solution, so they do not appear.

text:
A molecule has the structural formula \(\mathrm{HOCH_2CH_2CH{=}CHCOOH}\).
Which of these functional groups does it contain?
1 alkene
2 alcohol
3 carboxylic acid
4 ester
solution: Reading along: \(\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2}\) is a primary alcohol, \(\mathrm{CH{=}CH}\) is an alkene, and \(\mathrm{COOH}\) is a carboxylic acid. An ester needs a C(=O)-O-C link between two carbon groups, which this molecule does not have. 1, 2 and 3.

text:
Which three of these particles have the same electron arrangement?
1 Ar
2 \(\mathrm{K^+}\)
3 Ne
4 \(\mathrm{Na^+}\)
5 \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\)
[Atomic numbers: Ne = 10; Na = 11; Cl = 17; Ar = 18; K = 19]
solution: Count electrons: Ar 18, \(\mathrm{K^+}\) 19 - 1 = 18, Ne 10, \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) 11 - 1 = 10, \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) 17 + 1 = 18. The three with 18 (the argon arrangement) are 1, 2 and 5; Ne and \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) form a separate pair with 10.

text:
Dinitrogen tetroxide and nitrogen dioxide reach equilibrium in a closed container:
\[\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)} \qquad \Delta H = +58\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]
Which of the following would increase the amount of \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) at equilibrium?
1 raising the temperature
2 increasing the pressure by compressing the mixture
3 adding more \(\mathrm{N_2O_4}\)
4 adding a catalyst
solution: The forward reaction is endothermic, so heating shifts the equilibrium right (1). Compressing favours the side with fewer gas molecules, the left, so it reduces \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) (2 wrong). Adding reactant pushes the equilibrium right (3). A catalyst speeds up both directions equally and does not move the position (4 wrong). 1 and 3.

text:
Butane (\(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), \(M_r\) 58), propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\), \(M_r\) 58) and propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}\), \(M_r\) 60) are slowly warmed together from -50 °C at constant pressure.
In which order do they boil?
solution: With similar molar masses, the intermolecular forces decide. Butane is non-polar (London forces only) and boils first, at about -1 °C. Propanone is polar, adding dipole-dipole forces: about 56 °C. Propan-1-ol hydrogen-bonds through its O-H and boils last, at about 97 °C.

text:
A solution of potassium hydroxide has a concentration of 0.25 mol/L.
What is its concentration in g/L?
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1; O = 16; K = 39]
solution: \(M_r\) of KOH = 39 + 16 + 1 = 56. Grams per litre = moles per litre x molar mass = 0.25 x 56 = 14 g/L. 224 comes from dividing 56 by 0.25 instead of multiplying.

text:
Barium hydroxide, \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\), dissociates completely in water. What is the pH at 25 °C of a 0.050 mol/L solution?
[At 25 °C, \(K_w = [\mathrm{H^+}][\mathrm{OH^-}] = 10^{-14}\ \mathrm{mol^2\,L^{-2}}\)]
solution: Each formula unit releases two hydroxide ions, so \([\mathrm{OH^-}] = 2 \times 0.050 = 0.10\) mol/L. Then \([\mathrm{H^+}] = 10^{-14}/10^{-1} = 10^{-13}\) mol/L and pH = 13. Forgetting the factor of 2 gives about 12.7, nearest 12; 1.3 is the pOH of the undoubled value.

text: How many different structural isomers have the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_6Cl_2}\)?
solution: Three carbons can only form a straight chain, so the isomers differ in where the two chlorines sit: both on an end carbon (1,1-), both on the middle carbon (2,2-), one on an end and one in the middle (1,2-), or one on each end (1,3-). That is 4; 3,3- is the same as 1,1- counted from the other end.

text: How many protons (p), neutrons (n) and electrons (e) are in the ion \({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\)?
solution: The atomic number gives the protons: 26. Neutrons = mass number - protons = 56 - 26 = 30. A 2+ ion has lost two electrons: 26 - 2 = 24. The charge never changes the protons or neutrons.

text:
Which of the following molecules have bond angles of 120°?
[Atomic numbers: H = 1; B = 5; C = 6; F = 9]
1 \(\mathrm{BF_3}\)
2 \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) (ethene)
3 \(\mathrm{CH_4}\)
solution: Three electron regions around a central atom spread out flat at 120°. Boron in \(\mathrm{BF_3}\) has three bonds and no lone pair; each carbon in ethene has two single bonds and one double bond (three regions). Methane has four regions, giving 109.5°. 1 and 2 only.

text:
Here are five chromium species:
1 \(\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}\)
2 \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\)
3 \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\)
4 \(\mathrm{CrO_2}\)
5 \(\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\)
Which two have chromium in the same oxidation state?
solution: With O = -2: chromate \(\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}\): Cr - 8 = -2, so +6. Dichromate \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\): 2Cr - 14 = -2, so +6 each. \(\mathrm{CrO_2}\) is +4, and the simple ions are +3 and +2. Chromate and dichromate match.

subject: Mathematics
text:
The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are in the ratio 1 : 3, and the triangle covers 24 cm².
How long is its longest side?
solution: Let the shorter sides be \(a\) and \(3a\). Area \(= \tfrac{1}{2} \times a \times 3a = \tfrac{3}{2}a^2 = 24\), so \(a^2 = 16\) and \(a = 4\): the sides are 4 and 12. Hypotenuse \(= \sqrt{16 + 144} = \sqrt{160} = 4\sqrt{10}\) cm.

subject: Physics
text: Which physical quantity has the unit newton second (N s)?
solution: Force x time is impulse, which equals the change in momentum, so N s is a unit of momentum (the same as kg m/s, since 1 N = 1 kg m/s²). Work is N m (joules), power J/s (watts), pressure N/m² (pascals).

subject: Mathematics
text:
Simplify
\[\frac{3}{x^2 - 4} - \frac{1}{x + 2}\]
[where \(x \ne \pm 2\)]
solution: \(x^2 - 4 = (x-2)(x+2)\) is the common denominator. Rewrite the second fraction as \(\dfrac{x-2}{(x-2)(x+2)}\) and subtract: \(\dfrac{3 - (x - 2)}{x^2 - 4} = \dfrac{5 - x}{x^2 - 4}\). Forgetting to subtract the whole of \(x - 2\) gives \(1 - x\) on top.

subject: Mathematics
text:
The line \(\dfrac{x}{6} + \dfrac{y}{8} = 1\) cuts the x-axis at P and the y-axis at Q. A circle has PQ as a diameter.
What is the radius of the circle?
solution: Setting \(y = 0\) gives P = (6, 0) and setting \(x = 0\) gives Q = (0, 8). PQ \(= \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\) is the diameter, so the radius is 5, and the centre is the midpoint (3, 4).

subject: Physics
text:
A student has four 8.0 Ω resistors and may connect one or more of them in any arrangement. None is short-circuited.
What are the largest and the smallest resistances the student can make?
solution: All four in series give the most: 4 x 8.0 = 32 Ω. All four in parallel give the least: 8.0/4 = 2.0 Ω. Using fewer resistors can only give values in between.

subject: Physics
text:
A stone is thrown horizontally from the top of a cliff. Ignore air resistance.
Which of the following statements is/are correct while it falls?
1 Its horizontal velocity stays constant.
2 Its acceleration is constant and points straight down.
3 Its kinetic energy stays constant.
solution: The only force is the stone's weight, which is vertical and constant. So there is no horizontal force (1 is right) and the acceleration is g downwards throughout (2). Gravity does work on the stone as it falls, so its vertical speed and kinetic energy increase (3 wrong). 1 and 2 only.

subject: Mathematics
text:
\(p = 2 \times 10^{a}\) and \(q = 8 \times 10^{b}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
What is \(\dfrac{p}{q}\) in standard form?
solution: \(\dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{2}{8} \times 10^{a-b} = 0.25 \times 10^{a-b}\). Standard form needs a number from 1 to 10 in front, and \(0.25 = 2.5 \times 10^{-1}\), so it is \(2.5 \times 10^{a-b-1}\). Dividing powers subtracts the indices; it never divides them.
